artifact: Architect ruling: mounted guided-worker `rules` (C2b residual R-1), STUDIO-OBS-014 AC-1 clarification c
author: Aria (@architect)

ruling.summary: PO default adopted (option A). `rules` leaves the guided worker entirely: refused as a mounted key in every form including [], refused as a createGuidedServer option in every form, removed from GuidedRuntimeOptions, and the guided runtime builds its collector config with the constant rules: []. The structuralOnly-only alternative is rejected. Replay's TrustedPolicy.rules path is untouched. Fits the S3 unit with no contract change.
ruling.mountedConfig: guidedConfig.ts: remove 'rules' from MOUNTED_KEYS and from GuidedMountedConfig; add `insist(!Object.hasOwn(config, 'rules'), 'CONFIGURATION_DENIED')` next to the applicationPolicy refusal that s3-cutover.patch already adds. Every form is refused: a read rule, a structuralOnly rule, [], null, {}, false. One accepted config shape: the key is absent.
ruling.serverOption: transport.ts createGuidedServer: `insist(!Object.hasOwn(options, 'rules'), 'CONFIGURATION_DENIED')` beside the patch's applicationPolicy refusal. The option is refused in every form (including []), not silently dropped, so a caller that still passes it fails loudly. This applies the PO's 'refuses ... or drops' choice as 'refuses'.
ruling.runtime: guided/runtime.ts: delete `rules` from GuidedRuntimeOptions (:25) and build the ObservationConfig at :108 with the literal `rules: []`. With the type field gone, a smuggled option (untyped JS, cast) is inert, because the runtime never reads it. GuidedOwnership needs no separate check: it is reached only through createGuidedServer in production, and the runtime constant makes any leaked field inert.
ruling.guidedMain: guidedMain.ts:24 stops passing `rules: config.rules`. The entry point no longer contains the token `rules`.
ruling.notChanged: ObservationConfig.rules and CollectorOptions.rules (observationTypes.ts:47,56), the collector's rule logic (observationCollector.ts:201,222-226,321,419-433), observationSanitizer.ts:19,38, and observedReferencePolicy.ts:254-289 all stay. The replay adapter still feeds TrustedPolicy.rules to the same collector.
ruling.whyRefuseEmptyArray: Accepting [] (option C) would be functionally harmless, but it keeps two canonical forms of 'no rules' (absent and []), keeps a dead key that a later edit could quietly re-widen, and breaks the symmetry with the mounted applicationPolicy refusal, which is refused in every form (patch guidedMain.test.ts hunk: {..}, null, {}, false).

alternativeRejected.option: B: accept only structuralOnly mounted rules
reasons: It violates the binding outcome b(2). A structuralOnly rule still sets the exported node's policyRuleId (`rule?.policyRuleId ?? options.applicationPolicy?.policyRuleId`, observationCollector.ts:433) and its exported `name` (`rule?.name ?? displayName`, :432). The exported name is model-visible content that comes from an ungoverned file.

It violates the binding outcome b(3). `relevant = rule !== undefined || ...` (:428) exports a node that structural discovery would treat as irrelevant. `safe` also accepts `rule !== undefined` in place of a policy (:424). So a structuralOnly rule widens which nodes are exported.

Its one real benefit is the per-element veto ('an explicit structuralOnly field rule vetoes broader permission', README.md:678-679). It narrows only, but it is an ungoverned, unaudited narrowing. The governed object can already narrow by scoping a grant to a named role region (main, region or form). A governed per-testId veto would be a schema change, which AC-1 does not require (clarification c).
It leaves a mounted read-adjacent path whose classification check must be kept correct forever. Removing the path is the smaller, auditable surface.

lostInGuidedLearning: Exact data-testid reads of non-scalar elements (for example span/div). Governed region grants read visible text only from OUTPUT/DD/TD/role=status and the allowed field types (observationCollector.ts:228-231).
Per-element structuralOnly vetoes and the rule-supplied exported name.
Reads with no governed policy at all. After S3, applicationPolicy is required in the context anyway.
capabilityAccounting.verifiedNoProductionUser: git grep for the guided worker keys (callbackTokenFile, controllerCertificateFingerprint256) outside Java/tests/evidence finds only studio-runner/README.md, transport.ts, guidedMain.ts and two runner tests. No chart, values file or other deployment artifact in this repo writes a guided worker config. The loss is test-only in this repo. Deployment config lives in OBS-009 and must not add the key.
capabilityAccounting.replayInterplay: Replay keeps TrustedPolicy.rules (R-2 interim). If a TrustedPolicy holds a structuralOnly veto on a node that a governed grant made readable during learning, the learned read fails at replay with READ_REFUSED (observedReplay.ts:39-43). This fails closed and is already covered by the R-2 disclosure. It is not a new risk.
capabilityAccounting.residualForPo: RS-1. Whether GA needs exact-field reads of non-scalar elements in the governed document is a governed-schema change. It is not part of AC-1 or S3. Architect recommendation: do not add it pre-emptively. Decide on evidence from the OBS-010 20x3 benchmark applications: open it only if a benchmark value lives in a non-scalar element that no output/dd/td/status/field grant can reach. @po places it if needed (clarification c).

securityImplications: Closes the last read authorization that bypassed the hash-bound governed policy. After S3, every read the guided worker can perform is attributable to an approved, audited policy version whose hash the worker verified.

A compromised or misconfigured worker ConfigMap or secret mount can no longer grant reads, rename exported nodes or widen the export set. It can only stop the worker from starting (CONFIGURATION_DENIED).
Model-visible observation content (node names, classification, policyRuleId) now derives only from the DOM plus the governed policy. That matches the AC-2 data-flow description.
The mounted file stays trusted for TLS, JWT and callback material. That is out of scope and unchanged.

contractCheck.verdict: No contract change. Fits the S3 unit.
evidence: runner-context already cannot carry rules: c2b-spec fixture case 'runner-context / context / /applicationPolicy/rules = [] / SCHEMA'.

The only contract schema with `rules` is v3/replay-ipc.schema.json:107,125 (TrustedPolicy), which is replay and untouched. publication-fixtures.json:1836,2647 are TrustedPolicy literals and are untouched.

The mounted config, GuidedServerOptions and GuidedRuntimeOptions are internal TypeScript, not contract artifacts. The bridge refusal enum and openapi.yaml are untouched. CONFIGURATION_DENIED is a startup failure: guidedMain.ts:34 turns it into stderr GUIDED_WORKER_UNAVAILABLE and exit code 1. It is not a wire code.
No digest re-anchor, op-count pin or ADR-002 §13 row is owed for this change.

qaOracles: (1) Mounted refusal. Unit: parseGuidedMountedConfig refuses `rules` in each of the 7 forms listed under R14 with CONFIGURATION_DENIED. Process (any existing guidedMain-spawning IT, or a manual check): a worker.json with a permittedBusinessData or nonsecretApproved rule makes the process exit 1 with stderr GUIDED_WORKER_UNAVAILABLE, and the port never listens. Because structuralOnly is not kept, the 'structuralOnly accepted' branch of PO oracle (1) does not apply: a structuralOnly rule is refused too.
(1b) Server option: createGuidedServer with `rules` ([] or non-empty) throws CONFIGURATION_DENIED.

(2) Corrected vocabulary. PO oracle (2) names READ_REFUSED, but that is the replay code (observedReplay.ts). In guided learning, a read on a node with no governed read policy is refused at prepare with TARGET_CHANGED (runtime.ts:184), with no producer and no outcome. Runner oracles: the runtime.test inertness check (collector config rules == [] even when smuggled) and the converted guided-dataflow case (structuralOnly export, governed policyRuleId, no rule name, read refused at prepare).

(3) Static check on the three backend ITs: no `putArray("rules")` except GuidedPlanningIntegrationTest:328 and GuidedPublicationReplayIT:703 (both TrustedPolicy), and no `"order-policy"` / `"destination-policy"` literals. Runtime check: the three re-pointed bridge read cases pass with recipe policyRuleId 'business-read' and the worker.json has neither `rules` nor `applicationPolicy`.
(4) Static check on the runner: guidedMain.ts has no `rules` token, runtime.ts has no `options.rules`, and GuidedMountedConfig / GuidedRuntimeOptions have no `rules` member.

tradeOffs.choice: A refuse every form (chosen) vs C accept [] only
tradeOffs.pro: One config shape. Symmetric with the applicationPolicy refusal. No dormant key to re-widen.
tradeOffs.con: About 13 test literals lose `rules:[]`, and any out-of-repo worker.json carrying `rules: []` stops starting. Acceptable: Studio is unreleased, no compatibility layer exists (single-path decision), and there is no in-repo deployment config.
A loses the ungoverned per-element veto in guided learning. Region scoping in the governed policy narrows instead, and RS-1 records the GA question.

tradeOffs.choice: Refuse at createGuidedServer plus runtime constant vs runtime constant only
tradeOffs.pro: A loud failure at the production boundary, plus inertness for any other construction path.
tradeOffs.con: One extra insist and one more test. Negligible.

tradeOffs.choice: Re-point the bridge read cases vs drop them
tradeOffs.pro: Keeps the receipt, rollback and renewal coverage of a real read, now through the governed path.
tradeOffs.con: Touches the default fixture page, so every default-page test sees a <main> wrapper around the source. Mitigated by testId-based selection and the stop-on-name-failure rule.

autoDecisions: [AUTO-DECISION] Refuse or drop a `rules` server option? -> refuse in every form (reason: a silent drop hides a misconfigured caller; matches the applicationPolicy precedent in the patch).

[AUTO-DECISION] Drop any GuidedBridgeIntegrationTest case by name? -> none (reason: all three exact-rule read cases re-express through one region grant once the source becomes an output inside main 'Operations').

[AUTO-DECISION] One uniform governed policy for the bridge IT, or one per test? -> uniform (reason: a role grant is inert on pages without its anchor, so per-test switching adds seeding cost with no coverage gain).

[AUTO-DECISION] Correct PO oracle (2) code? -> yes, TARGET_CHANGED at prepare in guided; READ_REFUSED is replay vocabulary (reason: verified in runtime.ts:179-184 and observationCollector.ts:641-643).
